originality.rationale: The source paper arXiv:0708.3912 establishes the four-dimensional quantum-exterior algebra and Hochschild (co)homology but assumes a non-root-of-unity parameter; its conclusions do not cover the exterior resonance over finite fields. arXiv:0709.3029 treats Hochschild resolutions, not the square-zero ordinary-derivation compatibility variety. arXiv:1606.03119 gives broad complex derivation-matrix tables, which are credited as antecedents but neither computes commuting square-zero derivation tuple varieties nor finite-field rank polynomials. arXiv:1606.01727 studies Gerstenhaber brackets on Hochschild cohomology in characteristic zero, not literal derivation composition. arXiv:1001.0811 classifies commuting similarity classes of matrices, not algebra derivation tuples. Actual mathematical-index searches and all recoverable own-claim titles/claims were compared by object and implication; closest older own claims concern square-zero representations of the algebra (different objects) and characteristic-two square-zero derivations of the commutative Klein-four algebra (disjoint characteristics). The formula and non-equidimensional all-arity resonance are not implied by the inspected prior statements. Priority risk remains possible from unlocated stronger work.
residual_risks: Unlocated stronger result on commuting square-zero ordinary derivations may subsume the proof, especially a general exterior-algebra theorem.

value.rationale: The all-arity compatibility locus of literal square-zero associative derivations is natural for simultaneous differential structures on deformations of a small selfinjective algebra. Unlike an isolated count, the theorem gives a sharp deformation-parameter resonance: an affine space becomes a non-equidimensional two-component reduced variety for every tuple length ≥2; its complete finite-field rank polynomial, neighborhood spectra and maximal compatible planes all reflect this change. The precise family-wide invariant is not implied merely by a derivation-space dimension table.
